newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA may have destroyed data - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA may have destroyed data - WSJ.

text.p: The U.S. has evidence that Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp might have destroyed documents relating to the criminal investigation of the company, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing a federal prosecutor.
The paper said in its electronic edition that Kathleen Haley, the assistant U.S. attorney in charge of the probe, said the attempt to destroy the documents had already occurred.
She said the government has tape recordings from current Columbia employees who have been assisting law-enforcement officials. The employees had been wired with hidden microphones, she said.

Haley also said that more indictments are likely to come out of the investigation, which she said was broader and encompassed more issues and individuals than has been reported, according to the paper.
A spokesman from Columbia declined to comment, the paper said.
Last month, three Columbia officials were indicted in Florida on charges they defrauded the federal government by inflating reimbursement requests from Medicare and military health-care programs.
